findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The pre-check disk gate still counts the job's own idle producer build as used space
findings.evidence: `gate` sweeps only other jobs' idle build directories ("its own build directory is kept"). Under the plan, a job whose only shortfall is its own producer build is held as an environment stop at the gate, even though that directory would be removed a few lines later. The plan chose this order to keep tests built on `low_once_built` valid; that fixture (test_support.rs:706-721) reports low space only while some target/produce exists. Criterion 5 requires those tests to still pass, so the trade-off is defensible, and the hold clears itself when the next drain reclaims the directory. Fix: State the trade-off in the code comment and the changelog: the gate measures with the producer build still present, so a job can be held for one drain cycle that removing its own build would have saved. Alternatively, remove the build before the gate and change the low-disk fixture so it stays low until the `freed` marker exists. That would keep criterion 5's intent (work tree and candidate kept).

findings.summary: The criterion-2 demonstration names a fixture, FAILING_CHECK, that does not exist
findings.evidence: Searching crates/athena-core/src for FAILING_CHECK finds nothing. The same demonstration also says the check is a `sh -c` script that prints 300 lines, so the name looks like a slip. Fix: Name the real seam: a check leaked with `Box::leak` as `&'static [&'static str]` and passed to `athena_with`, as in the criterion-1 test.

findings.summary: Neither new test covers a cargo-test check (kind Test), where names come from `failed_tests`
findings.evidence: The `Docs` check is not a test kind, so `failed_tests` stays empty (checks.rs:409) and the `run::tests` test covers only the fallback that parses the output tail. In production the failing names come from `failed_tests`. The planned unit test of `log_entry` with `failed_tests` covers that path only at the unit level. Fix: Keep the `log_entry` unit test that uses `failed_tests` names, and assert in it that those names win over names parsed from the tail.

findings.summary: The 'drain log line' is shown through Athena::go's Ui rather than through a drain run
findings.evidence: The reading listed crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs as a deliverable. The plan puts the tests in core run/tests.rs and checks the `Lines` Ui. The drain prints the same `ctx.ui` lines, so this shows the behavior. Fix: In the change description, say that the drain prints the core Ui lines, so the core test's line is the drain log line.

summary: I checked the plan against the code, read-only. Its claims hold up. The checks line is built at crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs:1439-1451. The producer build directory is only removed after every check passes (mod.rs:1475-1489). `StateDir::remove_produce` exists (state.rs:269). `CheckRun` already has `output_tail` and `failed_tests`, so no new record type or allow-list entry is needed. `run_check` currently keeps the last 4096 bytes (checks.rs:25 and :431). The test helpers the plan names exist: `athena_with`, `counting` (which plants target/produce/debug/big), `low_once_built`, `recording_plenty_space` and `sh_spec`. Both new tests go through `Athena::go` and run real `sh` commands. Each would fail without the change: the criterion-1 check exits 1 while target/produce exists, and today's log line has no test name and the record holds at most 4096 bytes. Editing run/mod.rs and run/tests.rs is justified, because the check stage and the existing kept-on-failure test live there and drain.rs never sees check runs. I weighed Athena's two scope findings and agree they are minor. One design point is worth recording, though it does not block: the plan removes the build directory after the pre-check disk gate, so the gate still counts the job's own idle build as used space. I found no blocker or major problem.
